Build a feature graph for RABFA from the data

Source: R/rabfa.R
build_feature_graph.Rd

RABFA uses a graph of features (genes, proteins, metabolites) that are expected to act together, usually from a pathway database such as KEGG. When no such knowledge is available, this helper builds a data-driven graph by connecting features within the same view whose absolute correlation is at least cutoff, keeping at most max_neighbors strongest edges per feature. Prefer a knowledge-based graph when you have one: a graph learnt from the same data partly re-uses the signal.

Usage

build_feature_graph(X, cutoff = 0.5, max_neighbors = 5)

Arguments

X

Named list of features x samples matrices (or one matrix).

cutoff

Minimum absolute Pearson correlation for an edge (default 0.5).

max_neighbors

Maximum number of edges kept per feature (default 5).

Value

A data frame of edges with columns from and to, using "view::feature" names, ready for rabfa_graph.

Examples

sim <- simulate_multiomics(n_samples = 30, seed = 1)
g <- build_feature_graph(sim$data, cutoff = 0.6)
head(g)
#>                      from                      to
#> 1 transcriptome::gene_006 transcriptome::gene_015
#> 2 transcriptome::gene_010 transcriptome::gene_015
#> 3 transcriptome::gene_009 transcriptome::gene_017
#> 4 transcriptome::gene_001 transcriptome::gene_025
#> 5 transcriptome::gene_016 transcriptome::gene_031
#> 6 transcriptome::gene_009 transcriptome::gene_040
